questions.title: Chapman capture-recapture expectation and finite-sample bias in R
questions.description: Focused L0 known-result evaluation grounded in D. G. Chapman (1951) and the public CRAN recapr documentation. A closed population contains N labeled units. Conditional on fixed integer sample sizes 1<=n1,n2<=N, the first and second samples are independent uniformly chosen subsets without replacement, and M is their overlap. Thus M has the Hypergeometric(N,n1,n2) law. Develop one authoritative Markdown/LaTeX Theory workspace deriving the support and mass function of M and the Chapman estimator N_hat_C=(n1+1)(n2+1)/(M+1)-1. Starting from a shifted binomial-coefficient identity and Vandermonde's identity, derive an exact finite-N closed form for E[N_hat_C], its bias, and the condition under which the bias is exactly zero. Establish that the bias is never positive, explain why it is zero when n1+n2>=N and generally negative otherwise, derive P(M=0), and contrast the estimator's finite zero-overlap behavior with the undefined Lincoln-Petersen ratio n1*n2/M. Keep the finite-population sampling assumptions explicit and do not extend the claim to heterogeneous capture probabilities, mark loss, population change, dependent samples, confidence-interval validity, or novelty. The required model-authored artifact is est_chapman_capture_recapture and must implement the frozen run_estimator(request) contract as R source using language=r, execution_profile=scientific_wasm, and only base R. Do not substitute Python or call a capture-recapture package. Exploratory R may diagnose identities. A separately frozen confirmatory R assessment uses at least 12000 fresh hypergeometric replicates for each of three fully public designs: A=(N=60,n1=35,n2=30), B=(N=200,n1=40,n2=50), and C=(N=80,n1=8,n2=12). Before outcomes, freeze one seed per design, the exact estimator invocation, the exact expectation and exact variance obtained by summing the finite hypergeometric support, P(M=0), and all decisions. For every design, compare the empirical estimator mean with its exact expectation and the empirical zero-overlap frequency with its exact probability using four Monte Carlo standard errors. Confirm exact unbiasedness in A and downward bias in B and C. Simulation is implementation evidence, not proof. Source replication, novelty, and Lean formalization are not applicable, and unresolved theory, ABI, R execution, or empirical gaps must remain explicit.

primary_reference.title: Some Properties of the Hypergeometric Distribution with Applications to Zoological Sample Censuses
primary_reference.author: D. G. Chapman
primary_reference.venue: University of California Publications in Statistics

request_fields.name: first_sample_size
request_fields.shape: one finite integer-valued nonlogical R numeric scalar from 1 through 10000000
request_fields.edge_cases: Reject logical, character, nonnumeric, nonfinite, fractional, zero, negative, nonscalar, or above-limit values rather than coercing them.

request_fields.name: second_sample_size
request_fields.shape: one finite integer-valued nonlogical R numeric scalar from 1 through 10000000
request_fields.edge_cases: Reject logical, character, nonnumeric, nonfinite, fractional, zero, negative, nonscalar, or above-limit values rather than coercing them.

request_fields.name: overlap
request_fields.meaning: The observed overlap M between the two samples.
request_fields.shape: one finite integer-valued nonlogical R numeric scalar between zero and min(n1,n2)
request_fields.edge_cases: Zero is valid. Reject logical, character, nonnumeric, nonfinite, fractional, negative, nonscalar, or overlap larger than either sample size rather than coercing or clipping it.

response_fields.name: population_estimate
response_fields.edge_cases: At zero overlap the estimate remains finite and equals (n1+1)(n2+1)-1.
response_fields.normalization: No rounding or truncation; return the real-valued Chapman expression exactly up to floating-point arithmetic.

invariants.meaning: The request is a named R list containing exactly first_sample_size, second_sample_size, and overlap, and the response is a named R list containing exactly population_estimate. Missing, extra, malformed, or out-of-domain values are rejected rather than ignored or coerced.
Repeated calls with the same request return the same result and do not mutate the request, use random state, access files, invoke subprocesses, call the network, or depend on packages.
The response equals (first_sample_size+1)*(second_sample_size+1)/(overlap+1)-1 without rounding, truncation, or replacement by the Lincoln-Petersen ratio.
Swapping first_sample_size and second_sample_size while keeping overlap fixed leaves population_estimate unchanged.
For fixed sample sizes, population_estimate is strictly decreasing as an admitted overlap increases and is always at least max(first_sample_size,second_sample_size).
At overlap zero the estimate is (n1+1)(n2+1)-1; when n1=n2=overlap, it equals that common sample size.

empirical_claims.meaning: For each public design A, B, and C, freeze a fresh seed, at least 12000 independent Hypergeometric(N,n1,n2) overlaps, exact estimator invocation, the finite-support exact mean and variance of the estimator, exact P(M=0), and both four-MCSE decisions before confirmatory outcomes are revealed.

For every design, empirical mean(population_estimate) agrees with its exact finite-support expectation within four Monte Carlo standard errors of the mean, and the empirical zero-overlap frequency agrees with its exact hypergeometric probability within four binomial Monte Carlo standard errors.

The exact expectation equals N in design A because n1+n2>=N and is strictly below N in designs B and C; simulation must report these as exact-theory targets rather than infer the sign from noisy outcomes.

The assessment checks exact R source execution and finite-design behavior only. It is not a proof, a heterogeneous-capture result, an interval-calibration claim, a population-dynamics model, novelty evidence, or Lean evidence.

estimator_execution_contract.termination_guarantee: For every valid request, run_estimator performs a fixed finite number of scalar base-R operations and returns exactly one response without randomization, file access, network access, subprocesses, package installation, or request mutation.
